Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 83, verses 1–6:

Explanation of the words:

Wayl (ويل): a word of punishment, and a valley in Hell.

Lil-mutaffifin (للمطففين): those who diminish in measure or weight, who withhold from them both.

Idha iktalu 'ala al-nas (إذا اكتالوا على الناس): i.e., from people.

Yastawfun (يستوفون): the measure.

Wa-idha kaluhum (وإذا كالوهم): i.e., measured for them.

Aw wazanuhum (أو وزنوهم): i.e., weighed for them.

Yakhsirun (يخسرون): i.e., they diminish the measure or the weight.

Ala (ألا): an interrogative of reproach and denial.

Yazunn (يظن): i.e., is certain.

Li-yawm 'azim (ليوم عظيم): i.e., the Day of Resurrection, because of its terrors and the great matters within it.

Yawma yaqum al-nas (يوم يقوم الناس): i.e., from their graves.

Li-rabb al-'alamin (لرب العالمين): i.e., they will stand humbled and submissive, awaiting the judgment of God concerning them.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, "Woe to the defrauders" (ويل للمطففين): these are the first verses of Surah al-Mutaffifin. One of the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "We were the worst of people in measuring, to the extent that one of us would have two measures: one with which he buys and another with which he sells. But when [the verse] 'Woe to the defrauders' was revealed concerning us, we became the best of people in measure and weight." This noble companion spoke the truth. By Allah, when I arrived in Medina as a migrant in the year 1373 AH, I found them still as they had been, and I used to feel pity for them when they measured for me or weighed for me.

So His saying, "Woe to the defrauders" (ويْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ), threatens, glory be to Him, with a valley in Hell, with the pus-flow of the people of the Fire, those who cheat people of measure and weight, i.e., diminish it for them. He explains this by His saying, "Who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full" (ٱلَّذِينَ إذا ٱكْتالُواْ عَلى ٱلنّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ), i.e., when they buy from them, they take their measure full. Likewise when they weigh. "And when they measure for them or weigh for them, they diminish" (وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون), i.e., they diminish.

He, the Exalted, said, rebuking them and denouncing them: "Do not those think that they will be resurrected" (ألا يَظُنُّ أُوْلَٰئِكَ أنَّهُمْ مَّبْعُوثُونَ), from their graves, "for a tremendous Day" (لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ), which is the Day of Religion, recompense, and reckoning, "the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds" (يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلنّاسُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعالَمِينَ), humbled and submissive, awaiting His judgment concerning them. The standing will be prolonged for them a hundred years or more, and one of them will be bridled by his sweat, and among them is one whose sweat reaches halfway up his ears. The reports on this are numerous and authentic.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of defrauding in measure and weight, which is to take more, even a little, or to deliberately give less, even a little. What occurs without intent or purpose is among what is pardoned.

2- Reminder of the resurrection and recompense, and affirming them.

3- The greatness of the Day of Resurrection, the Day when mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds to judge between them and to recompense each person for his deeds, good or evil.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 83, verses 7–13:

Explanation of the words:

Kallā (كلا): that is, truly; and that the matter is not as those who cheat (al-mutaffifūn) imagine.

La-fī sijjīn (لفي سجين): Sijjīn is a proper name for the register (kitāb) of evil, in which the works of the devils and of the disbelievers are recorded. It is also a place at the bottom of the seventh earth, where the registers of the books are kept, and where the spirits of the wretched in general are.

Kitābun marqūm (كتاب مرقوم): that is, a written record, clearly inscribed, in which their deeds are set down.

Yawm al-dīn (يوم الدين): that is, the Day of Resurrection, which is the Day of Reckoning and Recompense.

Kull mu'tadin (كل معتد): that is, a wrongdoer who neglects the rights of his Lord, may He be exalted, and the rights of others.

Athīm (أثيم): one immersed in sins and who commits them frequently.

Asāṭīr al-awwalīn (أساطير الأولين): that is, the tales and reports written down by the ancients which are not authentic.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with a warning against wrongdoing and against deviating from the commands of the Lord, blessed and exalted. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Kallā﴾, means: the matter is not as the cheaters and those who defraud others of their rights imagine, that there is no precision in reckoning and recompense, or that such conduct is not recorded, nor called to account, nor requited, in truth. ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked﴾, that is, the wrongdoers who are corrupt in relation to the Sharia and its limits, ﴿is in Sijjīn﴾, a place at the lowest part of creation, where the spirits of the disbelievers and wrongdoers are, and the records of their deeds. His saying ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjīn is?﴾ means: and what would make you know, O our Messenger, what Sijjīn is, as an exaltation of its matter. His saying ﴿It is a register inscribed﴾ is an explanation of the record of the wicked: that it is a written, clearly inscribed record. ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾, that is, the painful punishment in the valley of Wayl on the Day of Resurrection for those who deny Allah, His signs, and the meeting with Him, and who deny the Day of Recompense and Reckoning. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And none deny it except every transgressor sinful﴾ means: none deny the Day of Recompense and Reckoning except every wrongdoer who transgresses the bounds, sinful, who commits sins and offences through his defiance of the commands of his Lord and his departure from obedience to Allah by committing the forbidden things. His saying ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the ancients"﴾ is an explanation of that transgressing sinner: that when the verses of Allah are recited to him, as a reminder and instruction, he rejects them by saying "Tales of the ancients", that is, these are the narratives and reports of the ancients, written down; and he denies the Book of Allah and rejects it.

Guidance from the verses:

1- An explanation of the record of the wicked, and that it is in Sijjīn. Explanation of the words:

ما كانوا يكسبون (ma kanu yaksibun): i.e., of sins and transgressions.

لمحجوبون (lamahjubun): i.e., they will be prevented from seeing their Lord until the Day of Resurrection.

لصالو الجحيم (lasalu al-jahim): i.e., they will enter it and be burned, tormented by it.

هذا الذي كنتم به تكذبون (hadha alladhi kuntum bihi tukadhdhibun): i.e., it will be said to them, as a rebuke and humiliation, while they are in punishment: "This is what you used to deny."

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to condemn transgression and the transgressors and sin and the sinners. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they have been earning has rusted over their hearts﴾. Rather, what has rusted over their hearts, i.e., covered and veiled them, is the effect of sins and crimes, which screened them from knowing the truth and accepting it. And His saying: ﴿Nay! Indeed they, from their Lord that Day, will be veiled﴾ means: as a deterrent and a restraint from their false statements and corrupt deeds, indeed they will be veiled from their Lord, so they will not see Him nor see His honor. ﴿Then indeed they will be burning in the Hellfire﴾, i.e., they will enter it and roast in its heat, tormented with various kinds of torment therein. Then it will be said to them, as a rebuke, humiliation and reproach: ﴿This is what you used to deny﴾, i.e., this punishment which you denied in the world, until you persisted in your disbelief and criminality, so there befell you what you are now in. So taste it; you will not increase except in punishment.

Guidance from the verses:

1. A warning against persisting in sins and not repenting from them, for this leads the servant to be deprived of repentance. In the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a servant sins, a black spot is made on his heart. If he repents, it is polished away; if he returns to sin, it grows until it covers his heart. That is the *ran* (rust) of which Allah said: Nay! Rather, what they have been earning has rusted over their hearts."

2. Affirmation of the vision of Allah the Exalted in the Hereafter, by His saying: "Indeed they, from their Lord that Day, will be veiled," meaning the wretched; hence the blessed are not veiled, and they will see their Lord. This is corroborated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾.

3. Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense.
